articles.title: Springs and Bounces in Native CSS
articles.description: Josh looks into how to approach using the linear() timing function for animations, and shares some pointers on the best approach to use them right now by “storing a handful of common timing functions in globally-available CSS variables”. As always, he includes plenty of interactive demos and code examples.
articles.author: Josh W. Comeau

articles.title: 🔒 Google Says It's (Almost) Time for HTTPS by Default
articles.description: Chrome 154 is expected to be released in October 2026 with “Always Use Secure Connections” enabled by default meaning users will get a warning if they try to access any non-https sites at all. Google explains its thinking here.
articles.author: Google Online Security Blog

articles.title: 🖼️ The Present and Potential Future of Progressive Image Rendering
articles.description: Just how useful is progressive image rendering today? Jake explores the current state of things (with demos) looking at various image formats (AVIF, JPEG XL, etc) across different browsers and varying network conditions.
articles.author: Jake Archibald

articles.title: Solved By Modern CSS: Section Layout
articles.description: Looks at how to approach building a fairly typical pattern, but making it dynamic with features such as clamp(), style queries, :has(), and more. A good, illustrated example of the potential modern CSS unlocks.
articles.author: Ahmad Shadeed

articles.title: The CSS Reset, Again
articles.description: Paweł looks at some popular resets crafted by others, picking out some highlights along with the rationale for using them.
articles.author: Paweł Grzybek

articles.title: For Your Convenience, This CSS Will Self-Destruct
articles.description: Scott shares a performance pleasing pattern he’s been using to make elements visible with a CSS keyframe animation in the event that JavaScript fails to do its thing.
articles.author: Scott Jehl

articles.title: ▶  Web MIDI, Web Audio, and What the Web Does Best
articles.description: A fun, and well explained, exploration of what Web MIDI, the Web Audio API and other tools can do when brought together. The end result? A creatively-coded take on Daft Punk’s 1997 hit ‘Around the World’.
articles.author: Katie Fenn

articles.title: CSS Layout Explained: Flexbox, Grid, Media Queries and Container Queries
articles.description: Part of Dr. Axel’s excellent, broader ‘web development for beginners’ series and a handy primer for CSS layout topics generally.
articles.author: Dr. Axel Rauschmayer

articles.title: The Man Who Keeps Predicting the Web’s Death
articles.description: “You can think the Web is dying or dead all you want. Many folks have said it over the years. But maybe don’t keep saying it periodically over a 30-year period, in constantly changing contexts”.
articles.author: Ernie Smith

articles.title: Page Headings Don’t Belong in the Header
articles.description: Some semantic pointers to keep in mind.
articles.author: Martin Underhill

articles.title: TypingSVG: Generate Animated SVGs to Represent Natural 'Typing' Effects
articles.description: An online tool that generates SVGs that show the process of typing some text that you supply. Has full Google Fonts support, lets you set typing speed and spacing on a line-by-line basis, supports backspacing, and more. A good eye catcher.
articles.author: whiteSHADOW1234

articles.title: 🎨 oklch.fyi: A One-Stop Resource for Learning About and Using OKLCH Colors
articles.description: If you’re new to the OKLCH color space, this is a good place to get started. Includes simple explanations as well as tools to create palettes, gradients, along with a gamut visualizer and color converter.
articles.author: Jakub Krehel

articles.title: uikit 1.0: Build 3D UIs in React Three Fiber Apps
articles.description: Ideal for games, XR (VR/AR), and web-based spatial-style apps. v1.0 takes some steps to align more closely with commonly accepted HTML/CSS behavior and techniques. GitHub repo.
articles.author: Poimandres

articles.title: Helium: A Small Library That Makes HTML Interactive
articles.description: Sort of like a lightweight HTMX or Alpine.js, allowing you to create simple interactive page elements without the usual JS overhead. Try some examples in this CodePen.
articles.author: Helium

articles.title: DevTUI: A Swiss-Army App for Developers
articles.description: Another option for a local, native all-in-one toolkit with things like encoders, decoders, formatters, converters, and more, but this one consolidates the utilities into a TUI and CLI.
articles.author: Stanislav Katkov
